newsitem.title: UK: Zinc prices seen at $1,400 and higher - Rudolf Wolff.
newsitem.headline: Zinc prices seen at $1,400 and higher - Rudolf Wolff.

text.p: Zinc prices are likely to climb in a "step" action in the medium to long term towards $1,400 and higher, brokers Rudolf Wolff said in a report on Friday.
Prices have eased in recent weeks from a rally high of $1,310 amid producer selling and fund profit taking.
But the dip is not surprising after zinc's 30 percent rally over the past six months, and prices should eventually bounce, analyst William Adams said in the report.
The new cycle of buying may include producers looking to buy back earlier short-term hedges, speculative bargain hunting, and funds deciding to top up.
Zinc continues to look bullish on the charts in the longer view, Adams said.
"In the short term prices look overbought, but the long term chart shows that $1,400 is the next target and then the next trading range would be $1,400-$1,600 plus," Adams said.
Support is expected to emerge between $1,180 and $1,200.
Zinc's fundamentals are equally constructive, Adams said, noting that total commercial stocks are at around seven weeks worth of consumption, while critical levels are six weeks.

"This would require another 120,000 tonnes stock to be drawn down before stocks hit critical levels. In 1997 a supply deficit of some 250,000 tonnes is forecast. A similar deficit is expected in 1998. Such a stock fall should push prices significantly higher," he said.
Three months prices on the London Metal Exchange (LME) were last at $1,245 per tonne, versus Thursday's close of $1,243.
